questions.question: What is the Causal Language Modeling (CLM) pre-training objective used by GPT?
options: Mask random tokens and predict them from bidirectional context
Predict each token given all previous tokens — next-token prediction
Translate text between languages
Classify documents by topic
questions.explanation: CLM (autoregressive language modeling) trains the model to predict token t given tokens 1..t-1. Every position in the sequence provides a training signal simultaneously, making it extremely data-efficient. This is the pretraining objective for all GPT models.

questions.question: How does GPT's attention differ from BERT's?
options: GPT uses cross-attention, BERT uses self-attention
GPT uses causal (masked) self-attention that can only attend to previous tokens; BERT uses full bidirectional attention
GPT uses multi-head attention, BERT uses single-head
They use identical attention mechanisms
questions.explanation: GPT applies a causal mask so token i can only attend to tokens 1..i. This unidirectional constraint enables autoregressive generation and means the model is trained using exactly the same mechanism used at inference time.

questions.question: What architectural changes distinguish GPT-2 from the original GPT?
options: GPT-2 uses cross-attention and a separate decoder
GPT-2 moved layer normalization to the input of each sublayer (Pre-LN) and used a modified weight initialization
GPT-2 replaced the FFN with convolutions
GPT-2 uses BERT's bidirectional attention
questions.explanation: GPT-2 key changes: Pre-LN (LayerNorm before sublayers for training stability), scaled weight initialization (multiplied by 1/√n_layers), larger context window (1024 tokens), and trained on WebText. These made training at scale more stable.

questions.question: What is 'few-shot prompting' as demonstrated by GPT-3?
options: Fine-tuning GPT on a few examples
Providing a few input-output examples in the prompt itself — the model infers the task pattern without weight updates
Training with a small dataset
Using a smaller model for efficiency
questions.explanation: GPT-3 showed that large language models can perform new tasks by showing a few examples in the prompt (in-context learning). The model's weights don't change — it just uses the examples as context to pattern-match on the task format.

questions.question: Why is temperature sampling important during GPT generation?
options: It controls the learning rate during training
It scales the logits before softmax: temperature < 1 sharpens the distribution (more deterministic), temperature > 1 flattens it (more random)
It determines how many tokens to generate
It controls the attention window size
questions.explanation: Dividing logits by temperature T before softmax: T→0 gives argmax (greedy), T=1 is the model's true distribution, T>1 flattens probabilities toward uniform (more creative/unpredictable). Temperature is a key knob for controlling generation diversity.
